approval.trigger: Public integrations start unpublished: 'the only Sentry organization that will be able to see or install it will be the organization that created the integration'. Publication is a review submission done by email: clicking 'Publish' next to the integration 'sends an email to integrations-platform@sentry.io, letting us know your integration is ready for review'. Once published, the integration is listed for all Sentry users. Requirements documented on the page read are content/logo requirements; no review duration, SLA, or criteria beyond those are stated.
approval.wait: Not stated (no review duration or SLA published in the docs read)

blockers.detail: Unpublished means your org only, and going public is an email-triggered manual review with no documented timeline or checklist on the page read. This is the schedule risk for launch.
blockers.howToClear: No documented fast path; submit with the content and logo requirements fully met and plan launch timing around an unknown queue.
blockers.title: Opaque, manual publication gate

blockers.detail: 'Public integrations generate authentication tokens after a successful OAuth installation. These tokens automatically expire every eight hours, meaning they must be refreshed manually.' Your backend must run refresh reliably per installation, forever.
blockers.howToClear: Implement refresh from day one; prefer Sentry's recommended manual refresh (below) over the plain exchange.
blockers.title: 8-hour token expiry for public integrations

blockers.detail: Sentry notes refreshes can commit on Sentry's side while the new token is 'lost in transmission', which is why they recommend the manual refresh method: a JWT signed with your client secret (iss/sub = client_id, exp = now+60s, jti = UUID) sent as Bearer with grant_type 'urn:sentry:params:oauth:grant-type:jwt-bearer', instead of the standard refresh_token exchange at the same endpoint.
blockers.howToClear: Use the JWT-bearer manual refresh as your primary path.
blockers.title: Lost-refresh anomaly

alternatives: Internal integration (custom to one organization; no OAuth flow, an org-wide auth token immediately on creation, auto-installed on your org; right for your own org, wrong for multi-customer)

Generic OAuth2 user tokens (authorization code grant at sentry.io/oauth/authorize and /oauth/token, PKCE S256 recommended, plus a device authorization grant for headless/CLI; tokens are per-user and single-org, distinct from installation tokens)
flavor.recommended: A public integration (Sentry app) on the Integration Platform, installed per organization with an OAuth installation flow
flavor.why: Public integrations are built for 'the general public of Sentry users', installable by any Sentry organization once published, and they require an OAuth flow: after a user installs and approves permissions, Sentry issues a grant code + installation ID to exchange for an organization-scoped installation token. Permissions are org-scoped scopes (org/project/team/member/event read/write/admin) applied across the whole installing organization, and 'you can't create an integration or change an existing integration to have permissions greater than your own user settings'.

humanMust: Create the public integration in Settings > Developer Settings and make the permission/webhook/redirect configuration decisions
Supply the mandatory logo (and icon if using UI components)
Click Publish to trigger the review email when ready
name: Sentry
nuances: Tokens are installation/org-scoped, not per-user, for public integrations; users approve the full permission set at install, with no documented per-project or partial-consent subsetting.

The generic OAuth2 flow differs: its access tokens expire after 30 days, device codes expire in 600 seconds with a 5-second default polling interval, and a token only covers the specific organization the user selected during the flow.
Internal-integration tokens 'do not expire automatically', capped at 20 tokens per internal integration.

Logo is mandatory for public integrations: PNG, 256x256 to 1024x1024 px, transparent background unless it fills the space. With UI components an icon is also required: PNG RGBA, same size range, 'All pixels must be black or transparent'.
Browser use of tokens is limited to origins listed in 'Authorized JavaScript Origins' (one per line, no protocol, no wildcards; subdomains listed individually).

Verify Install: if enabled, your service must PUT status 'installed' to complete setup, and you should handle installation.deleted webhooks on uninstall. To receive alert webhooks, the webhook URL must be set AND the integration selected as the 'Send a notification via <your integration>' alert action.
prerequisites: The integration's permissions (scopes), webhook URL, and redirect URL decided
A logo to spec (mandatory for public integrations)

steps.detail: In sentry.io: Settings > Developer Settings, create a new integration and choose 'public'. Configure name/description. It starts unpublished: only your organization can see or install it.
steps.title: Create a public integration

steps.detail: Set the permissions (scopes) the integration needs (Sentry prompts users to approve these at installation; you cannot request more than your own user's permissions). Specify the webhook URL for resource events, optionally toggle 'Alert Action', add UI components if any, configure the redirect URL, and enable 'Verify Install' if your service does post-install finalization.
steps.title: Configure permissions, webhooks, redirect

steps.detail: Mandatory for public integrations: PNG, 256x256 to 1024x1024 px, transparent background unless it fills the space. If you use UI components, an icon too: PNG RGBA, same size range, all pixels black or transparent.
steps.title: Upload the required logo (and icon)

steps.detail: Users install from the Integrations page or your fixed external-install URL (sentry.io/sentry-apps/<slug>/external-install/). After the user approves all permissions, Sentry sends a grant code + installation ID via the installation.created webhook or as query params (code, installationId) on your redirect URL. Your /setup endpoint POSTs to sentry.io/api/0/sentry-app-installations/{installationId}/authorizations/ with grant_type authorization_code, code, client_id, client_secret; store the installation ID, token, and refreshToken per installation. If Verify Install is on, PUT status 'installed' to complete.
steps.title: Build the install/OAuth backend

steps.detail: Installation tokens expire every 8 hours. Refresh at the same authorizations endpoint, preferably via Sentry's recommended manual refresh: a JWT signed with your client secret (iss/sub = client_id, iat, exp = now+60s, jti = UUID) as Bearer, with grant_type 'urn:sentry:params:oauth:grant-type:jwt-bearer'. Also handle installation.deleted webhooks on uninstall.
steps.title: Run the 8-hour refresh cycle

steps.detail: Click 'Publish' next to the integration; this emails integrations-platform@sentry.io that your integration is ready for review. Once published it is listed for all Sentry users. No review timeline is stated in the docs.
steps.time: One click; review duration not stated
steps.title: Publish for review

tagline: Two gates stack up: your integration is visible only to your own organization until an email-triggered manual review publishes it (no timeline stated), and once live, its tokens expire every eight hours, so refresh is a permanent backend duty.

time.active: ~30 min of configuration + ~half a day of install/refresh backend
time.total: Unknown: the publication review has no stated duration
